candidates.oneLine: Open-source doc-testing framework: parses testable actions out of your doc text/specs and executes them against the real product (browser/API), emitting PASS/FAIL JSON.
candidates.whyRelevant: This is the closest analog to terse:audit's core move — it doesn't opine on prose, it MEASURES documentation against ground truth (actual product behavior) the same way audit measures docs against the code. Could compose as a second, execution-based failure class alongside audit's LLM-reader-comprehension failures (lie/placement/findability) — a 'stale-instruction' class caught by running the steps, not asking a model to answer questions.
candidates.evidence: repo pushed_at 2026-08-26 (via gh api), 131 stars, README.md read directly: 'You write tests, and Doc Detective runs them directly against your product to make sure your docs match your user experience... results (PASS/FAIL and context) are output as a JSON object.' Companion npm package doc-detective-core and doc-detective/agent-tools repo (13 stars) ship agent/skill wrappers.

candidates.oneLine: A Claude Code skill (.skills/docs-reorg/SKILL.md) that scores a doc page against the four Diataxis types plus a wayfinding/landing type, flags mixed-content pages, and emits a machine-readable split plan.
candidates.whyRelevant: The strongest 'Diataxis in rule-shaped, agent-followable form' I found — it turns the (originally prose-only) Diataxis framework into a scoring rubric with a confidence table and diagnostic signals (verb-mood shifts, one-job-vs-many, step teaching-vs-instructing), rather than just describing the taxonomy. Could feed terse:audit as a pre-pass that classifies which Diataxis bucket a doc claims to be, before scoring reader questions against it.
candidates.evidence: Read repo file tree (contents API): .skills/docs-reorg/{README.md,SKILL.md,references}. Read SKILL.md in full via gh api + base64 decode — it defines a 4-step workflow (Read / Classify into a confidence table / Split plan / Nav-shape for MkDocs) and cites references/page-types.md and references/reasoning.md for diagnostic signals. 6 stars, pushed 2026-05-27. Not a measurement of reader success, only a structural classifier — still opinion-shaped, but the opinion is externalized as a followable rubric, not prose to intuit.

coverageNotes:
Covered via gh api/gh search (all evidence is either a file I opened with contents API + base64 decode, or repo metadata via gh api): Diataxis (trogera/diataxisSkills classifier, thegooddocsproject/templates, anivar's 27-rule blend), Google dev-doc style guide (vale-cli/Google confirmed live + fresh, textlint-rule-preset-google as a stale second attempt), Microsoft Writing Style Guide (vale-cli/Microsoft), GOV.UK content design (alphagov/gds-vale-styles, stale), plain-language standards (GSA/plainlanguage.gov source found but not rule-shaped; ISO 24495-1 no artifact found), Write the Docs (repo found, prose-only), docs-as-code toolchains (folded into the Vale-based entries plus doc-detective, which is the standout because it tests against real product behavior rather than opining on prose), minimalism/Carroll and Information Mapping (no artifacts found, recorded as ideas per instruction).

What this angle could not reach: I did not open thegooddocsproject/templates' individual per-type folders beyond the top-level README, did not check writethedocs/www's internal guide/ pages for a hidden checklist, and did not verify the current text of ISO 24495-1 itself (paywalled). WebFetch to vale.sh/hub timed out once; I recovered the same fact (vale-cli/Google, formerly errata-ai/Google) via WebSearch instead and cross-checked it with gh api, so that claim is doubly sourced. I did not search non-GitHub artifact hosts (npm-only packages, Hugging Face, GitLab) beyond one WebSearch pass, so a Diataxis-as-JSON-schema or ISO-24495-as-checklist artifact could exist there and be missed.
dropped: Dropped without a slot: testthedocs/vale-styles (48 stars) and vale-cli/packages — general Vale-style aggregators/hubs, redundant once the specific Google/Microsoft/GDS packages were confirmed individually, and squarely in the already-rejected 'prose linter' bucket with no measurement angle. Dropped keithpatton/diataxis-agent-skill (17 stars) and PeterKnego/diataxis-docs-skill (11 stars) — same category as trogera/diataxisSkills (Diataxis-as-Claude-skill) but I only opened trogera's SKILL.md in full; the other two are likely near-duplicates and including all three would crowd out distinct methodologies. Did not pursue readability-formula tools (Flesch-Kincaid calculators, Hemingway-style scorers) — these measure surface sentence complexity, not reader comprehension or code-truth, and felt like a weaker fit than doc-detective for the 'measures a document' criterion; flagging here in case that class is still of interest on a follow-up pass.
